title: Exam 1 (do this last)
blurb: Exam 1 practice. Work the week 1 and week 2 tests first.

questions.prompt: In the stress response, the release of ADH (antidiuretic hormone) results in
questions.suggestedRationale: ADH retains water, which increases circulating blood volume.

questions.prompt: Which Factors would decrease host resistance?
questions.suggestedRationale: Broken skin is a portal of entry and lowers host resistance.

questions.prompt: Which area of the body is considered sterile
questions.suggestedRationale: Brain tissue is normally sterile; skin, perineum, and the nasal cavity have flora.

questions.prompt: When a person is exposed to an antigen for a second time, their immune system will respond in which way?
questions.suggestedLabel: B. have a more rapid response
questions.suggestedRationale: Re-exposure produces a faster, stronger secondary immune response.

questions.prompt: Which infection of the dermis and subcutaneous tissue is often caused by staphylococcus aureus secondary to injury or ulcer?
questions.suggestedRationale: Cellulitis is infection of the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, often by S. aureus after a break in the skin.

questions.prompt: Which condition is likely to lead to metabolic alkalosis?
options: Early stages or initial stages of vomitting
questions.suggestedLabel: B. Early stages or initial stages of vomitting
questions.suggestedRationale: Early vomiting loses gastric acid and can cause metabolic alkalosis; the other conditions cause acidosis.

questions.prompt: Which type of skin cancer grows quickly and metastasizes to lymph and other organs?
questions.suggestedRationale: Malignant melanoma grows quickly and metastasizes to lymph nodes and distant organs.

questions.prompt: Macrophages are a type of cell involved in
questions.suggestedRationale: Macrophages are a key part of nonspecific (innate) immunity, though they also present antigen later.

questions.prompt: Which stress hormone is produced in the adrenal cortex?
questions.suggestedRationale: Cortisol is made in the adrenal cortex; epinephrine comes from the medulla, and ACTH/ADH are pituitary.

questions.prompt: Pemphigus is caused by?
questions.suggestedRationale: Pemphigus is an autoimmune blistering disease.

questions.prompt: What would be an example of Secondary Prevention?
options: Wearing a seatbelt in car for safety
Maintaining a healthy diet to control and manage Diabetes Type 1
Getting a scan or checked for a form of cancer due to family history
questions.suggestedLabel: D. Getting a scan or checked for a form of cancer due to family history
questions.suggestedRationale: Screening (a cancer scan because of family history) is secondary prevention; seatbelts and vaccines are primary, and managing known diabetes is tertiary.

questions.prompt: Our body has different types of defense mechanism, Inflammation helps in the healing process, where does it fall?
options: Immunoglobulins that help attack specific antigens or microbe.
questions.suggestedRationale: Inflammation is a nonspecific (innate) defense.

questions.prompt: Our body has Lymphocytes, and there are two types, which type of cell can produce antibodies?
questions.suggestedRationale: B lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells that produce antibodies.

questions.prompt: What is pathophysiology?
options: Study of diseases at the community level
Study of functional or physiological changes in the body due to disease
questions.suggestedLabel: C. Study of functional or physiological changes in the body due to disease
questions.suggestedRationale: Pathophysiology studies the functional changes in the body caused by disease.

questions.prompt: What does "idiopathic" mean in relation to disease causes?
questions.suggestedRationale: Idiopathic means the cause is unknown.

questions.prompt: What type of necrosis occurs when cell proteins are altered, leading to coagulation?
questions.suggestedRationale: Coagulative necrosis is denaturation of cell proteins, typical of ischemic infarcts.

questions.prompt: What type of acid-base imbalance is caused by excessive bicarbonate loss?
questions.suggestedRationale: Loss of bicarbonate produces metabolic acidosis.

questions.prompt: Which condition is characterized by increased cardiac contractions and kidney stones?
questions.suggestedRationale: Hypercalcemia strengthens cardiac contractions and predisposes to kidney stones.

questions.prompt: Which chemical is released by injured cells to activate pain receptors?
questions.suggestedRationale: Bradykinin from injured tissue activates pain receptors (prostaglandins mainly sensitize them).

questions.prompt: What is a primary cause of redness and warmth during inflammation?
options: Increased blood flow to the damaged area
Leakage of protein into interstitial spaces
questions.suggestedLabel: B. Increased blood flow to the damaged area
questions.suggestedRationale: Redness and warmth come from increased blood flow (hyperemia) to the injured area.

questions.prompt: Which systemic effect is commonly associated with extensive inflammation?
questions.suggestedRationale: Fever (pyrexia) is the classic systemic feature of extensive inflammation.

questions.prompt: What is a potential complication of chronic inflammation?
options: Formation of a granuloma or scar tissue
questions.suggestedLabel: A. Formation of a granuloma or scar tissue
questions.suggestedRationale: Chronic inflammation may end in granuloma or scar formation.

questions.prompt: Which type of burn involves the destruction of all skin layers and often underlying tissues?
options: Full-thickness burn ( Third or fourth Degree)
questions.suggestedLabel: C. Full-thickness burn ( Third or fourth Degree)
questions.suggestedRationale: A full-thickness (third- or fourth-degree) burn destroys all skin layers and may involve deeper tissue.

questions.prompt: What characterizes scar tissue?
questions.suggestedRationale: Scar tissue is nonelastic and does not restore original function.

questions.prompt: What type of microorganism requires living tissue to survive and replicate?
questions.suggestedRationale: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites and need living host cells to replicate.

questions.prompt: Which bacteria shape is described as spherical?
questions.suggestedRationale: Cocci are spherical bacteria.

questions.prompt: What is a characteristic of endotoxins?
options: Released on the death of gram-negative bacteria
questions.suggestedLabel: C. Released on the death of gram-negative bacteria
questions.suggestedRationale: Endotoxins are LPS released when gram-negative bacteria die.

questions.prompt: What is the most common method of transmission for rickettsiae infections?
questions.suggestedRationale: Rickettsiae are typically spread by insect (arthropod) vectors.

questions.prompt: What is the first stage of an infectious disease?
questions.suggestedRationale: The incubation period is the first stage, from exposure until symptoms begin.

questions.prompt: What type of antimicrobial drug inhibits the reproduction of bacteria?
questions.suggestedRationale: Bacteriostatic drugs inhibit bacterial reproduction; bactericidal drugs kill bacteria.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a key characteristic of prions?
questions.suggestedLabel: C. Cause degenerative nervous system diseases
questions.suggestedRationale: Prions cause degenerative neurologic diseases (for example, Creutzfeldt-Jakob) and have no nucleic acid.

questions.prompt: What type of immunity involves the production of antibodies?
questions.suggestedRationale: Antibody production is humoral immunity.

questions.prompt: What is the role of macrophages in the immune system?
options: Initiate the immune response by presenting antigens
questions.suggestedLabel: B. Initiate the immune response by presenting antigens
questions.suggestedRationale: Macrophages initiate the adaptive response by processing and presenting antigen.

questions.prompt: Which immunoglobulin is involved in allergic responses?
questions.suggestedRationale: IgE mediates allergic (type I) responses.

questions.prompt: What is the first antibody to increase during an immune response?
questions.suggestedRationale: IgM is the first antibody to rise in a primary immune response.

questions.prompt: What is an example of a Type I hypersensitivity reaction?
questions.suggestedRationale: Allergic rhinitis is a classic type I hypersensitivity.

questions.prompt: Which cells are responsible for cell-mediated immunity?
questions.suggestedRationale: T lymphocytes carry out cell-mediated immunity.

questions.prompt: What is the primary cause of anaphylactic shock?
options: Rapid release of histamine causing systemic effects
questions.suggestedLabel: B. Rapid release of histamine causing systemic effects
questions.suggestedRationale: Anaphylactic shock is caused by massive, rapid histamine release with systemic vasodilation.

questions.prompt: Which organ is responsible for the maturation of T lymphocytes?
Which autoimmune disease is marked by the characteristic “butterfly rash”?
questions.suggestedRationale: The malar 'butterfly' rash is characteristic of systemic lupus erythematosus.

questions.prompt: What type of hypersensitivity reaction causes contact dermatitis?
questions.suggestedRationale: Contact dermatitis is a type IV delayed hypersensitivity.

questions.prompt: Which skin disorder is marked by silvery plaques and excessive keratinocyte proliferation?
questions.suggestedRationale: Psoriasis produces silvery plaques from excessive keratinocyte proliferation.

questions.prompt: What is the causative agent of impetigo?
questions.suggestedRationale: Impetigo is most often caused by Staphylococcus aureus; Streptococcus pyogenes can also cause it, so this item is slightly ambiguous.

questions.prompt: What is the primary cause of warts (verrucae)?
questions.suggestedRationale: Warts (verrucae) are caused by human papillomavirus.

questions.prompt: What is the most common early symptom of acute necrotizing fasciitis?
options: Severe pain in the infected area
questions.suggestedLabel: B. Severe pain in the infected area
questions.suggestedRationale: Severe pain out of proportion to early skin findings is the usual first symptom of necrotizing fasciitis.

questions.prompt: Which type of fungal infection affects the scalp?
questions.suggestedRationale: Tinea capitis is fungal infection of the scalp.

questions.prompt: Which skin condition is characterized by the autoimmune destruction of cohesion between epidermal cells?
questions.suggestedRationale: Pemphigus is autoimmune loss of cohesion between epidermal cells, causing blisters.

questions.prompt: What is the primary symptom of scabies?
options: Intense itching and tiny burrow marks on the skin
Thickened, cracked skin on the feet
questions.suggestedLabel: B. Intense itching and tiny burrow marks on the skin
questions.suggestedRationale: Scabies presents with intense pruritus and fine burrow tracks.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an early sign of malignant melanoma?
options: A lesion with irregular borders and color changes
questions.suggestedLabel: C. A lesion with irregular borders and color changes
questions.suggestedRationale: An early melanoma warning is a lesion with irregular borders and color variation (ABCDE).

questions.prompt: Which skin disorder is characterized by hard, shiny, tight, immovable areas of skin and may lead to organ failure in severe cases?
questions.suggestedRationale: Scleroderma causes tight, shiny, bound-down skin and can progress to internal organ fibrosis.
